checkpoints.description: Task 'keystone-weave-v1' completed successfully.
[1/4] Plan: seeded terminal graph + hack/alert state -> World dungeon gate/hunter response/hash -> network nodes and links in the dungeon scene -> docs, ADR and gates

impact_assessment.why: Cyberpulse's network and living-alert model gives the dungeon an objective beyond reaching the exit and makes combat respond to player actions.
impact_assessment.benefits: Every dungeon run gets a deterministic infiltration graph, a risk/reward alert clock and hunter pressure, all replayable through the harness.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: World snapshot/hash and dungeon interact gain network state; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: single-thread; state: hacking must remain reachable and exit gating must not strand a run.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Generate terminals only in reachable non-spawn/exit rooms, test graph connectivity, force completion in replay tests, and keep a sealed-exit message with the current progress.

checkpoints.description: Task 'keystone-space-v1' completed successfully.
[1/3] Plan: inventory current modules -> define core vs games boundary and GameModule contract -> document dependency rules, module roadmap, refactor sequence and ADR

impact_assessment.why: Combat, light locks, weave, networks and space are game content; treating them as engine core conflates feature breadth with engine depth and blocks a reusable API.
impact_assessment.benefits: A reviewable core contract, a clean future refactor path, and no further genre feature work until the boundary is accepted.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: no runtime API changes yet; dependency: docs only; concurrency: single writer; state: no code moves before review.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Freeze feature work, classify every module, state acceptance criteria, and keep the current tree runnable until the refactor is approved.

checkpoints.description: [3/3] Architecture review package complete: core/module boundary, GameModule contract, dependency rules, module inventory/roadmap, staged refactor plan, ADR-012 and README status note; 6/6 gates; checklists: passed

handoff.next: user review of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, then the GameModule/Engine boundary refactor

checkpoints.description: Task 'keystone-architecture-v1' completed successfully.

[1/5] Plan: add core runtime (GameModule, input, clock, replay, serialization, physics) -> refactor Engine/CLI/sample -> remove game modules/tests/assets -> rewrite docs/ADR/config -> gates, screenshot and commit

impact_assessment.why: The project is crowded with game mechanics and lacks a reusable engine boundary; the user directed a game-agnostic core and removal of those modules.
impact_assessment.benefits: A small, testable engine core that external games import; no genre code in the package; clear plugin and replay contracts.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: Engine API changes and game code is deleted; dependency: stdlib only for new core modules; concurrency: single-thread loop; state: keep the core runnable after each step.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Build the core boundary first, keep the sample runnable, remove modules only after tests/CLI pass, and regenerate maps/docs/ADR.

checkpoints.description: Task 'keystone-core-reset-v1' completed successfully.
[1/4] Plan: no-GL simulation + action scripts -> frame report (pixel stats, scene bounds) -> CLI --simulate/--report and docs -> gates, ADR and commit

impact_assessment.why: AIKit, headless CI and model-based UI analysis need machine-readable simulation and frame evidence, not only a window and a PNG.
impact_assessment.benefits: The engine can be driven and verified without a GPU/window, and a model receives structured image and scene data alongside the screenshot.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new headless/analysis APIs and CLI flags; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: single-thread; state: actions and reports must be deterministic.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Test actions, hashes and report schemas; keep the rendered path unchanged; validate pixels and scene projections.

checkpoints.description: Task 'keystone-ai-runtime-v1' completed successfully.
[1/3] Plan: describe_game + --describe -> testing helpers for deterministic scenarios -> report comparison API -> docs, gates and commit

impact_assessment.why: AI clients need discovery, repeatable assertions and before/after graphics comparisons, not only a simulation command and a one-off report.
impact_assessment.benefits: A model can discover the action schema, verify a scenario deterministically and compare frame reports without guessing.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: adds core discovery/testing/compare APIs; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: single-thread; state: no new game modules.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Test describe/loader, double-run hashes and report diffs; keep the no-GL path; run all gates.
